latin: P. Dominus vobiscum. R. Et cum spiritu tuo. P. Sequentia (vel initium) sancti Evangelii secundum, &c. R. Gloria tibi Domine.
notes: Facing Latin and English columns resume at the head of xxi after the full-measure English of xx. One printed block containing the greeting and the announcement of the Gospel; the Latin abbreviates the evangelist's name by `&c.` as the English does.

latin: R. Laus tibi, Christe.
notes: The Latin occupies one line where the English takes two.

latin: CREDO in unum Deum Patrem omnipotentem, factorem cœli et terræ, visibilium omnium et invisibilium.
notes: Two-line drop C with `REDO` in capitals, given here as CREDO. The book prints no speaker for the Creed. `cœli` with the oe-ligature and `terræ` with the ae-ligature.

latin: Et in unum Dominum Jesum Christum, Filium Dei unigenitum, et ex Patre natum ante omnia sæcula. Deum de Deo: Lumen de Lumine; Deum verum de Deo vero; genitum non factum; consubstantialem Patri, per quem omnia facta sunt. Qui propter nos homines, et propter nostram salutem descendit de cœlis. Et incarnatus est de Spiritu Sancto, ex Maria Virgine: ET HOMO FACTUS EST*. Crucifixus etiam pro nobis sub Pontio Pilato, passus et sepultus est. Et resurrexit tertia die secundum Scripturas. Et ascendit in cœlum, sedet ad dexteram Patris. Et iterum venturus est cum gloria judicare vivos et mortuos; cujus regni non erit finis.
notes: Runs over the page break xxi/xxii, breaking in the Latin at `ex Maria Vir-` / `gine`. `ET HOMO FACTUS EST` is set in full capitals, matching the English column; the asterisk after it is the book's own and keys the footnote at the foot of xxii. Heavy inking at the head of xxii fills the s and e of `sepultus`, which is read from the surviving strokes and not repaired from any other book.

latin: Et in Spiritum Sanctum, Dominum et vivificantem, qui ex Patre Filioque procedit: qui cum Patre et Filio simul adoratur, et conglorificatur; qui locutus est per prophetas. Et unam sanctam Catholicam et Apostolicam Ecclesiam. Confiteor unum Baptisma in remissionem peccatorum. Et expecto resurrectionem mortuorum, et vitam venturi sæculi. Amen.
notes: This printing carries the Filioque: `qui ex Patre Filioque procedit`. It prints `Et expecto`, with expecto and not exspecto, the word standing whole and unbroken on its own line. `sæculi` with the ae-ligature. `Amen.` italic.

latin: P. Dominus vobiscum. R. Et cum spiritu tuo.
notes: Set in the facing columns immediately after the Creed. The `Oremus` that completes this greeting is carried over to the head of xxiii and is entered separately at seq 20.

latin: Oremus.
notes: Italic in both columns, set as the first line of xxiii. No response is printed; the block completes the greeting at the foot of xxii.

latin: Suscipe, sancte Pater, omnipotens æterne Deus, hanc immaculatam Hostiam, quam ego indignus famulus tuus offero tibi Deo meo vivo et vero, pro innumerabilibus peccatis, offensionibus et negligentiis meis, et pro omnibus circumstantibus; sed et pro omnibus fidelibus Christianis, vivis atque defunctis; ut mihi et illis proficiat ad salutem in vitam æternam. Amen.
notes: `æterne`, `æternam` with the ae-ligature. `Hostiam` capitalised as printed. `Amen.` italic.

latin: Deus qui humanæ substantiæ dignitatem mirabiliter condidisti, et mirabilius reformasti; da nobis per hujus Aquæ et Vini Mysterium, ejus divinitatis esse consortes, qui humanitatis nostræ fieri dignatus est particeps, Jesus Christus Filius tuus Dominus noster: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus sancti Deus; per omnia sæcula sæculorum. Amen.
notes: `Aquæ`, `Vini` and `Mysterium` capitalised as printed; `sancti` lower-case in `Spiritus sancti Deus`. `hujus`, `ejus` with j. `Amen.` italic.

latin: Offerimus tibi, Domine, calicem, salutaris, tuam deprecantes clementiam: ut in conspectu divinæ Majestatis tuæ, pro nostra et totius mundi salute cum odore suavitatis ascendat. Amen.
notes: The Latin column prints a comma after `calicem` which the received text does not carry, and it is transcribed as printed. The u of `tuam` is a failed sort, printing as a raised mark between t and am; the word is given whole and the damage named here rather than repaired from another book. `Amen.` italic.

latin: In spiritu humilitatis, et in animo contrito suscipiamur a te, Domine: et sic fiat sacrificium nostrum in conspectu tuo nodie, ut placeat tibi, Domine Deus.
notes: The Latin column misprints `nodie` for `hodie`: the letter is an n, with no ascender, read at 200 per cent magnification against the h of `hoc` on the same page. Transcribed as printed and not corrected.

latin: Veni, sanctificator, omnipotens æterne Deus, et benedic hoc sacrificium tuo sancto nomini præparatum.
notes: `æterne` and `præparatum` with the ae-ligature. No cross glyph is printed in this Latin block.

latin: Per intercessionem beati Michaelis archangeli stantis a dexteris Altaris Incensi, et omnium electorum suorum, incensum istud dignetur Dominus benedicere, et in odorem suavitatis accipere. Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
notes: `Altaris Incensi` capitalised as printed. `Amen.` italic.

latin: Incensum istud a te benedictum, ascendat ad te Domine, et descendat super nos misericordia tua.

Dirigatur, Domine, oratio mea, sicut incensum, in conspectu tuo: elevatio manuum mearum sacrificium vespertinum. Pone Domine custodiam ori meo, et ostium circumstantiæ labiis meis: ut non declinet cor meum in verba malitiæ, ad excusandas excusationes in peccatis.
notes: `circumstantiæ` and `malitiæ` with the ae-ligature. The block ends at `in peccatis.` and the book prints no doxology here.

latin: Lavabo inter innocentes manus meas: et circumdabo altare tuum, Domine.
notes: The Lavabo verses stand as separate printed blocks in this book, one per verse, and are transcribed one to a row as the sibling English artifact divides them.

latin: Ut audiam vocem laudis: et enarrem universa mirabilia tua.
Domine dilexi decorem domus tuæ, et locum habitationis gloriæ tuæ.
notes: `tuæ` and `gloriæ` with the ae-ligature.

latin: Ne perdas cum impiis animam meam; et cum viris sanguinum vitam meam.
notes: Runs over the page break xxv/xxvi, breaking after `et cum` at the foot of xxv.

latin: In quorum manibus iniquitates sunt: dextera eorum repleta est muneribus.
Ego autem in innocentia mea ingressus sum: redime me, et miserere mei.
Pes meus stetit in directo: in ecclesiis benedicam te Domine.
Gloria Patri, et Filio, &c.
notes: DIFFERS FROM THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: the doxology is abbreviated to its first words and `&c.` in the Latin column as in the English, where the Ordo Missae sets it out in full. No `Sicut erat` clause is printed, and nothing is supplied.

latin: Suscipe sancta Trinitas hanc oblationem, quam tibi offerimus ob memoriam Passionis, Resurrectionis, et Ascensionis Jesu Christi Domini nostri: et in honorem beatæ Mariæ semper Virginis, et beati Joannis Baptistæ, et sanctorum Apostolorum Petri et Pauli, et istorum, et omnium Sanctorum: ut illis proficiat ad honorem, nobis autem ad salutem: et illi pro nobis intercedere dignentur in cœlis, quorum memoriam agimus in terris. Per eumdem, &c. Amen.
notes: The conclusion is abbreviated `Per eumdem, &c.` in the Latin column. `cœlis` with the oe-ligature. `Amen.` italic.

latin: Orate Fratres: ut meum ac vestrum sacrificium acceptabile fiat apud Deum patrem omnipotentem.
notes: Neither column prefixes this block with a speaker mark, though the response that follows is prefixed `R.` in both. `Fratres` capitalised and `patrem` lower-case, as printed.

latin: R. Suscipiat Dominus sacrificium de manibus tuis ad laudem et gloriam nominis sui, ad utilitatem quoque nostram, totiusque Ecclesiæ suæ sanctæ.
notes: The Latin prints a comma after `nominis sui` where the facing English prints none after `name`.

latin: P. Per omnia sæcula. sæculorum. R. Amen.
notes: The Latin runs over two lines, `P. Per omnia sæcula.` and then `sæculorum. R. Amen.`; the full stop after `sæcula` is the printing's own error and is transcribed as printed. `Amen.` italic.

latin: P. Dominus vobiscum. R. Et cum spiritu tuo. P. Sursum corda. R. Habemus ad Dominum. P. Gratias agamus Domino Deo nostro. R. Dignum et justum est.
notes: The whole Preface dialogue is set as one continuous block in each column, with the P. and R. run in. This is the last block on xxvii.
